INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) - RENEWABLE FUTURES: JUNIOR HIGH SCHOOL AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT CENTER

THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DESIGN AND CONSTRUCT A NEW GUYMON JUNIOR HIGH SCHOOL IN GUYMON, OKLAHOMA, THAT MEETS SCHOOL DISTRICT AND COMMUNITY EXPECTATIONS AND OBJECTIVES; PROVIDES EDUCATIONAL PROGRAMMING TO PREPARE STUDENTS FOR GREEN-SECTOR CAREERS; USES ENVIRONMENTALLY FRIENDLY DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION PROCESSES TO PROVIDE ECONOMIC BENEFITS TO THE COMMUNITY; AND SERVES AS A CATALYST FOR CONTINUED GROWTH AND DEVELOPMENT IN GUYMON. THE OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT ARE TO ENSURE THAT THE SCHOOL DISTRICT IS ADEQUATELY PREPARED TO BEGIN THE RENEWABLE FUTURES PROJECT; ENSURE THAT THE SCHOOL BUILDING DESIGN PROCESS IS COMPLETE; COMPLETE ALL REQUIRED CONSTRUCTION ACTIVITIES TO SUCCESSFULLY OPEN AND OPERATE THE SCHOOL SITE; AND TO ENSURE THAT COMMUNITY AND STUDENT PROGRAMMING, AS WELL AS CONSTRUCTION, DESIGN, AND ECONOMIC OUTCOMES, MEET COMMUNITY NEEDS AND OBJECTIVES.

INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) - SOUTHEASTERN MONTANA TRANSMISSION SITING AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT (SM-TSED) INITIATIVE

THIS PROJECT AIMS TO PROVIDE RURAL AND DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES IN SOUTHEASTERN MONTANA WITH FEDERAL FUNDING FOR CRITICAL INFRASTRUCTURE. IT WILL FOSTER COLLABORATION AMONG COUNTIES AND TRIBES AND WILL PROMOTE COMMUNITY AND ECONOMIC GROWTH IN AREAS LIKE CLEAN ENERGY AND EMERGENCY SERVICES. THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH SUB-GRANTS TO FUND COUNTY AND TRIBAL PROJECTS AFFECTED BY THE NORTH PLAINS CONNECTOR CONSTRUCTION. THE PROJECT AIMS TO FOSTER COOPERATION AND ADDRESS INFRASTRUCTURE NEEDS, DEVELOPING GUIDELINES WITH INPUT FROM COUNTIES AND THE TRIBE.

INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) - PROPEL NY ENERGY SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITIES INITIATIVE

PARTNERS WILL ALSO REACH 1,000 COMMUNITY MEMBERS, ESPECIALLY AMONG UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS, THROUGH TARGETED OUTREACH AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT TO INFORM THEM ABOUT TRAINING AND EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES.

INFLATION REDUCTION ACT (IRA) - JOINT AGENCY PATH TO STREAMLINE TRANSMISSION SITING IN ILLINOIS

THE STATE OF ILLINOIS, THROUGH THE ILLINOIS COMMERCE COMMISSION (ICC) AND THE ILLINOIS DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES (IDNR), PROPOSE TO LAUNCH A COMPREHENSIVE INITIATIVE TO STREAMLINE AND EASE TRANSMISSION LINE SITING REVIEW AND APPROVAL PROCESSES IN ILLINOIS, ENSURE BETTER PROTECTION OF NATURAL AND HISTORICAL SITES AND RESOURCES, AND INCORPORATE COMMUNITY-IDENTIFIED NEEDS INTO THE SITING APPROVAL PROCESS. THE INITIATIVE WILL FOCUS ON UPGRADING ICC AND IDNR REVIEW AND BASELINE DATA POINTS TO BE USED FOR THE $1.4 BILLION, 380-MILE MISO LRTP TRANCHE 1 AS WELL AS THE LRTP TRANCHE 2 PROJECTS WITH OVERLAPPING IMPACT AREAS IN ILLINOIS. THE IMPROVEMENTS AND DATA COLLECTED WILL THEN INFORM AND EASE ANY FUTURE ICC AND IDNR TRANSMISSION PROJECTS SITING REVIEW AND DECISIONS AND LOWER COSTS AND TIME FOR PROJECT DEVELOPMENT AND REVIEW.

THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH AND OPERATE THE SANTA YNEZ CHUMASH OCEANOGRAPHIC INSTITUTE (THE “OCEANOGRAPHIC INSTITUTE” OR “INSTITUTE”), A CULTURAL AND SCIENTIFIC ORGANIZATION THAT ADVANCES THE SOCIO-ECONOMIC AND CULTURAL FUTURE OF THE SANTA YNEZ CHUMASH AND OTHER CHUMASH TRIBES. THE INSTITUTE WILL TRAIN AND EDUCATE MEMBERS OF THE CHUMASH. TRIBES WILL ENGAGE, CONSULT, COLLABORATE, AND CO-MANAGE THE USE AND PROTECTION OF COASTAL MARINE AREAS.  THE PROJECT WILL INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF THE CHUMASH TO EDUCATE AND TRAIN TRIBAL MEMBERS IN OCEAN AND COASTAL POLICY AND SCIENCE; DEVELOP THE TRIBE’S CAPABILITY TO ENGAGE AS CO-MANAGERS AND COLLABORATORS IN THE FUTURE PLANNING AND MANAGEMENT OF THE NEWLY DESIGNATED CHUMASH HERITAGE NATIONAL MARINE SANCTUARY; AND ESTABLISH AN INTERDISCIPLINARY EDUCATION PROGRAM TO TRAIN TRIBAL PROFESSIONALS WHO CAN ADVISE INDUSTRIES AND AGENCIES RESPONSIBLE FOR THE SITING, PERMITTING, OPERATIONS AND MAINTENANCE OF VARIOUS OCEAN AND COASTAL ACTIVITIES SUCH AS OFFSHORE WIND ENERGY AND OFFSHORE TRANSMISSION PROJECTS.
